A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PROPS research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite substantial revisions and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original MuJoCo and discrete-action learning experiments, sampling-error measurements, and ablations in Section 6 and Appendices D–G.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds GridWorld evaluations, bias/variance analyses, and runtime measurements in Section 6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: V2 corrects the written clipped loss from min[-g, clip(-g,...)] in v1 Equation 4 to min[-g, -clip(g,...)] in v2 Equation 5. This aligns the formula with clipping behavior already described in v1's prose and Table 1. Algorithms 1–2, KL regularization, and buffer reuse remain unchanged; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: V2 adds a tabular 5×5 GridWorld with competing terminal goals, enabling fixed-policy and policy-learning evaluations. The six MuJoCo environments and CartPole, LunarLander, and Discrete2D100 tasks remain covered.

E2.justification: V1 excludes ROS from policy-learning comparisons. V2 evaluates PPO-ROS against PPO-PROPS and PPO during GridWorld learning in Figure 5a. The existing MuJoCo comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation protocols for GridWorld visitation-distribution error, true-gradient cosine similarity, and success rates, including learning with b=1 and 80-transition batches. It also introduces runtime comparisons. Section 6.1 changes the stated fixed-policy initialization from expert to random while reusing the earlier plot, so this reported setting revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic analysis by directly relating sampling error to gradient accuracy, examining visitation-distribution bias and variance, and measuring computational overhead. These analyses address questions beyond v1's return and sampling-error comparisons. The existing clipping, regularization, buffer-size, and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 adds explicit bias/variance estimators and three-run runtime means with standard errors. It changes Figure 10's band description from one standard error to 95% bootstrap intervals despite retaining the graphic. The reused main training-error plot is labeled with 5 rather than 50 seeds, matching the appendix; these reporting changes do not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds GridWorld gradient-accuracy and learning results: PROPS and ROS reach 100% success, versus approximately 77% for PPO in the text and about 80% in Figure 5a. New runtime results show PROPS taking up to about twice PPO-BUFFER's time under their tuned settings. MuJoCo performance-profile curves are also modestly revised, while the principal benchmark rankings and most appendix plots are retained.

T1.justification: V2 adds a convergence proposition in Section 4 and its proof in Appendix A, absent from v1. It presents almost-sure convergence of empirical state visitation for the ideal most-under-sampled-action rule under finite spaces and irreducibility, extending the stated scope beyond the earlier DAG assumption. This is distinct from proving convergence of the implemented PROPS algorithm.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly adds increasing the fraction of runs reaching high-return policies to its contribution list and experimental question Q2. The central claims about reducing sampling error and improving data efficiency through adaptive off-policy sampling remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains why ROS matches PROPS in fixed-policy tabular experiments, why sampling-error differences diminish as policies become deterministic, and why learning two policies increases runtime. It also introduces an empirical unbiasedness interpretation in Appendix D.1. The principal discussion limitations, including ignoring actions' gradient importance, are retained.

D1.justification: V2 discloses the runtime hardware, a MacBook Air with an M1 CPU, and selected HalfCheetah update intervals of 4096 steps for PPO-BUFFER and 1024 for PPO. Tables 2–3 retain the main implementation settings. Conversely, v1's explicit fixed-policy specification of m=256, a 64m buffer, and 128m collected samples is no longer supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds Achiam (2018) and Silver (2015), removes Liu et al. (2018), and positions its new convergence proposition as relaxing Zhong et al.'s DAG assumption. The broader related-work organization and positioning relative to exploration, policy evaluation, and sample-reuse methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is reorganized, Section 4's extended Swimmer motivation is replaced, and experiments gain explicit metric, setup, and results blocks. The appendices are substantially reorganized, including consolidating former Appendices D–G under Appendix D and adding a contents page. These changes extend beyond inserting new scientific material.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the overview diagram, removes the Swimmer illustration and individual-run display, combines the earlier main sampling-error plots into Figure 3, and adds GridWorld, bias/variance, and runtime figures. Algorithms become narrower wrapped displays, performance profiles lose median guide lines, and appendix figures are extensively rearranged.

improvement.justification: The GridWorld gradient-accuracy and learning evidence, runtime measurements, and corrected clipping formula provide useful gains over v1. However, Equation 10's signed average bias necessarily cancels for normalized distributions, so it cannot support the new unbiasedness claim; Equation 11 measures mean-squared error without establishing unbiasedness. These statistical flaws and inconsistent descriptions of reused experiments limit the overall improvement.
